scope.edition: Classic English El Grande base rules
scope.excluded: Expansions; summaries; question banks; answer keys; readers; other review reports
scope.inspection: Read relevant base-rule text and visually inspected complete PDF pages 9 and 10; printed card images confirm the wording differences.

source_references.section: The Action Cards — Detailed explanations of the card texts
source_references.evidence: If the meaning of a special action is not clear, consult the detailed explanation of that card.

source_references.section: The following applies to all cards, A
source_references.evidence: Only moving the King can change the King’s region; players may neither add to nor take from that region.

source_references.section: The following applies to all cards, B
source_references.evidence: If an action card requires the secret disk, the players each simultaneously and secretly select a region using the disks.

source_references.section: 2 stack — The King returns! bold heading
source_references.evidence: Your fellow players each must send 3 Caballeros back to the provinces. Each can take them from any regions and/or from his court.

source_references.section: 2 stack — The King returns! explanatory paragraph
source_references.evidence: Each player, starting with the player to the left of the player who played the special action and continuing clockwise around the table, must send 3 of his own Caballeros back to the provinces. The players may not take Caballeros from the King’s region or the Castillo.

source_references.section: Left-margin printed The King returns! card image
source_references.evidence: Each player must send 3 Caballeros back to the provinces. Each can take them from any regions and/or from his court.

source_references.section: 2 stack — secretly remove 2, bold heading and printed card image
source_references.evidence: Your fellow players must remove 2 of their own Caballeros from any region and send them back to the provinces. Decide secretly!

All players must simultaneously select a region with their secret disks. The selected region must contain at least 2 of their Caballeros. If a player only has at most one Caballero in any region then he must select such a region. The players may not take Caballeros from the King’s region or the Castillo.

source_references.section: 2 stack — secretly return all from one region, bold heading and printed card image
source_references.evidence: Your fellow players must send all of their own Caballeros from one region back to the provinces. Each player decides which region. Decide secretly!

source_references.section: 2 stack — secretly return all from one region, explanatory paragraph
source_references.evidence: All players must simultaneously select a region with their secret disks. The selected region must contain at least 1 of their Caballeros. If a player has no Caballeros in any region, he is not affected. The players may not take Caballeros from the King’s region or the Castillo.

source_references.section: 2 stack — Decay of Authority, return 3 from court
source_references.evidence: Any player with fewer than 3 Caballeros in his court sends all Caballeros in his court to the provinces.

conclusions.question: Does the selecting player also return 3 Caballeros?
conclusions.answer: Yes. There is sufficient authority within this base rulebook to state that each player, including the actor, returns 3 own Caballeros when the special action is executed and sufficient eligible Caballeros exist.
conclusions.order: Start with the player to the actor’s left and proceed clockwise through each player; the actor is therefore last.
conclusions.eligibility: Pieces may come from multiple regions and/or the player’s court, excluding the King’s region and the Castillo.
conclusions.reason: The detailed instruction expressly imposes the return on each player, and the printed card independently agrees. The p7 instruction directs readers to the detailed explanation when meaning is unclear. Only the bold heading uses fellow players.
conclusions.remaining_gap: The source does not explicitly call its conflicting bold heading an error, and does not specify a shortfall rule for this action. The heading conflict should be acknowledged, but it does not prevent an actor-included conclusion.

conclusions.question: Does secretly removing 2 affect the actor’s Caballeros?
conclusions.answer: The best-supported removal scope is the actor’s fellow players only. Do not assert that the actor also removes 2 merely because the next paragraph says all players select a region.
conclusions.reason: Both the bold action instruction and its printed card explicitly assign removal to fellow players. The detailed paragraph’s all players sentence describes simultaneous disk selection; it does not explicitly assign removal to the actor. This differs materially from The King returns, where both the detailed removal obligation and printed card say each player.
conclusions.confidence: high for the printed removal instruction; procedural participation remains ambiguous
conclusions.remaining_gap: All players literally includes the actor for disk selection and the paragraph also imposes a qualifying-region condition. The text never explicitly says whether the actor makes a harmless selection, is exempt from selecting, or is included by an unintended change of removal scope. Preserve that procedural inconsistency rather than silently turning it into an actor-removal rule.

conclusions.question: Does secretly returning all own Caballeros from one region affect the actor?
conclusions.answer: The best-supported removal scope is the actor’s fellow players only. All players in the explanatory paragraph specifies disk selection, and is not an explicit instruction that the actor returns pieces.
conclusions.reason: The bold action instruction and the printed card agree on fellow players. The explanatory paragraph does not explicitly replace that removal scope; its all players language describes how regions are chosen.
conclusions.eligibility: Each affected player chooses a region containing at least 1 own Caballero. A player with no Caballeros in any region is explicitly unaffected. No pieces may be taken from the King’s region or Castillo.
conclusions.confidence: high for the printed removal instruction; procedural participation remains ambiguous
conclusions.remaining_gap: The actor’s literal inclusion in all players disk selection and its eligibility requirements is not reconciled with fellow players removal scope. Do not present the actor’s disk obligation or exemption as definitively resolved.

unresolved_issues.issue: The King returns requires 3 but supplies no explicit instruction for a player with fewer than 3 eligible pieces across non-King regions and court.
unresolved_issues.limit: The same page explicitly handles a shortfall for Decay of Authority, but does not state that this exception generalizes. Do not invent a return-as-many-as-possible rule as an express rule of The King returns.

unresolved_issues.issue: The remove-2 paragraph relaxes the 2-piece condition when the player has at most 1 in any region, but does not expressly explain zero-piece cases or a player whose only region pieces are in the King’s region.
unresolved_issues.limit: The protected-location prohibition is explicit. The source does not permit taking protected pieces and does not clearly specify a legal region choice or exact shortfall procedure in these edge cases.

unresolved_issues.issue: The all-from-one-region paragraph exempts a player with no pieces in any region, but does not explicitly exempt or give a selection procedure for a player whose only region pieces are in the King’s region.
unresolved_issues.limit: Returning pieces from the King’s region remains prohibited; do not invent an exception or an additional exemption.

unresolved_issues.issue: For both secret removals, fellow players receive the removal obligation while all players receive the simultaneous-selection instruction. The source does not explicitly reconcile those scopes.
unresolved_issues.limit: Opponents-only removal is directly supported by card and heading. Claiming the actor also removes pieces, or that the actor definitely does not select a disk, goes beyond an explicit resolved statement in this source.

editorial_recommendation: State The King returns as affecting every player, actor included, and cite the detailed paragraph plus printed card. State both secret removal effects as applying to fellow players; describe their simultaneous secret choice without declaring actor participation resolved. If actor disk participation or insufficient eligible pieces is tested, flag the source gap rather than fabricate a definitive answer.
